question.text: Under the PMLA framework, the minimum retention period for PMS client identification and account documents is:

answer.text: One year from the date of the transaction
Three years from the date of opening the account
Five years after the business relationship ends or the account is closed, whichever is later
Ten years from the date of opening the account

explanation.text: The Logic: Under the PMLA framework, records pertaining to client identification and account files must be preserved for at least five years after the business relationship between the client and the reporting entity has ended or the account has been closed, whichever is later. The Trap: Shorter periods (one or three years) understate the obligation and fixed periods like ten years from account opening misstate the trigger; the clock runs from the end of the relationship/account closure, not from account opening. Note: PMS books and records have their own separate retention requirement (the immediately preceding five accounting years under the PMS regulations); do not conflate the PMLA client-document rule with the PMS books-of-account rule.
